text: LORD, you are my God; I will exalt you, I will praise your name, for you have done wonders—plans formed long ago, carried out in perfect faithfulness.
For you have turned the city into a heap of rubble, the fortified town into a ruin; the stronghold of foreigners is a city no longer, never to be rebuilt.

versions.text: You have turned the city into a heap of rubble, the fortified town into a ruin; the stronghold of foreigners is a city no longer, never to be rebuilt.
versions.explanation: The opening כִּי ("for") links this verse to the praise of verse 1 as its ground. Dropping it breaks the logical flow that the Hebrew establishes, and restoring it also helps the oral cadence of the sequence.

text: Therefore a strong people will honor you; the city of ruthless nations will fear you.

versions.text: Therefore a strong people will honor you; the cities of ruthless nations will fear you.
versions.explanation: קִרְיַת is singular ("city"), parallel to the singular collective "a strong people" in the first line. The plural "cities" both departs from the Hebrew and breaks the parallelism.

text: For you have been a refuge to the poor, a refuge to the needy in their distress, a shelter from the storm, a shade from the heat. For the breath of the ruthless is like a storm beating on a wall,
like heat in a parched land. You silence the uproar of foreigners; as the shadow of a cloud subdues the heat, so the song of the ruthless is stilled.
On this mountain the LORD of hosts will prepare for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wine—the finest of foods, the purest of wines.
On this mountain he will destroy the shroud that veils all peoples, the sheet that covers all nations.
He will swallow up death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face and remove the disgrace of his people from all the earth, for the LORD has spoken.
On that day it will be said: "Look, this is our God; we waited for him, and he has saved us. This is the LORD; we waited for him. Let us rejoice and be glad in his salvation."
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain, but Moab will be trampled underfoot as straw is trampled down in a pit of dung.
Moab will spread out his hands in the midst of it, as a swimmer spreads his hands to swim, but the LORD will bring down his pride along with the cunning of his hands.

versions.text: There he will spread out his hands, as a swimmer spreads his hands to swim, but the LORD will bring down his pride along with the cunning of his hands.
versions.explanation: In the current wording the first "he" most naturally reads as the LORD from verse 10, whereas in Hebrew it is Moab flailing in the dung pit; naming Moab removes the ambiguity for a listener and preserves בְּקִרְבּוֹ ("in the midst of it").

text: Your high, fortified walls he will bring down, lay low, and cast to the ground, into the dust.
